prompts: Users of our harness plugins report that tool.after hooks run out of order, that sometimes a hook never runs, and that a failing hook is silently ignored. The hook bus and the plugin are in {WS}; the README there says how the bus must behave. Fix the bus. Its public API stays as it is, the tests in {WS}/test stay as they are, and package.json takes no dependencies.
answers:
[goal] Fix the hook bus so `tool.after` handlers run in order, always run, and failing hooks reject `emit`.

[action] The bug was in `emit` in `src/bus.ts`: it used `list.forEach(async handler => { await handler(payload); })`. `forEach` does not await, so (1) all handlers started concurrently — no subscription order, (2) `emit` resolved before any handler finished, and (3) rejections were unhandled, so a failing hook was silently ignored. The fix: snapshot the handler list at emit start (so mid-emit unsubscription doesn't stop the current emit, per the README), then `for...of` with `await handler(payload)` — sequential, first rejection rejects `emit`, later handlers skipped. No API change, no dependency, tests untouched.

[result] `npm test`: 2 pass, 0 fail. A separate end-to-end script (run, then deleted) verified against the README contract: plugin order notice → redaction → audit on `tool.after`, notice only on the first emit, async handlers run in subscription order (later-subscribed slower handler doesn't overtake), a throwing handler rejects `emit` with the same error and later handlers don't run, mid-emit unsubscribe still runs the rest of that emit but not the next, and `emit` resolves only after the last handler settles. Output: "all plugin/bus checks passed".

[next] None — the fix is in `src/bus.ts` `emit` only, and the workspace is clean (no browser tabs or apps were opened).
